result.rationale: The diff shows `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in embed.js — a substring containment check rather than strict origin equality. Depending on whether discourseUrl ends with '/', an attacker-controlled origin like 'https://forum.example.com.evil.com' (or any string containing the configured discourseUrl) passes the check and can send discourse-resize messages to arbitrarily resize the iframe. The insecure-substring origin check mechanism is verifiable in the diff; exploitability depends on the configured URL format, so confidence is moderate.

judged_text: The postMessage origin check uses a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of equality, so any origin whose string contains discourseUrl as a substring is accepted as a trusted sender. An attacker page hosted at e.g. https://forum.example.com.attacker.com (or attacker.com?x=https://forum.example.com-style substrings) passes the check and can postMessage {type:'discourse-resize', height:...} to resize the embedded comments iframe arbitrarily (UI defacement / clickjacking-layout manipulation inside the embedding page).

record.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check uses a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of equality, so any origin whose string contains discourseUrl as a substring is accepted as a trusted sender. An attacker page hosted at e.g. https://forum.example.com.attacker.com (or attacker.com?x=https://forum.example.com-style substrings) passes the check and can postMessage {type:'discourse-resize', height:...} to resize the embedded comments iframe arbitrarily (UI defacement / clickjacking-layout manipulation inside the embedding page).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which only accepts messages when the *origin string* (`e.origin`, e.g. `https://forum.example.com`) is a substring of `discourseUrl`. The finding claims the opposite (that any origin containing `discourseUrl` as a substring is accepted, e.g. `https://forum.example.com.attacker.com`), but that would be rejected because `"https://forum.example.com".indexOf("https://forum.example.com.attacker.com") === -1`. So the described bypass/attack does not follow from the diff.
